correctness.rationale: Every finite centered dilation acts diagonally in the Gaussian Fock monomial basis. A bounded Toeplitz symbol has bounded angular average h(t), whose Laplace transform is holomorphic on Re z<1 and equals the finite rational eigenvalue generating function near zero. Its distinct simple poles have residues -c_j/lambda_j, so none may lie in that half-plane. Along -R, the Laplace transform tends to zero, eliminating any nonzero coefficient of C_0. For all permitted parameters the explicit bounded radial Gaussian symbol has exact k-th moment lambda^k, proving sufficiency; Berezin Gaussian convolution injectivity gives uniqueness. Distinct lambda^n yield the polynomial rule, Weyl equidistribution and elementary positive-cosine residue counts yield the densities, and exact finite-order case splits yield the multiplication boundary. The full analytic proof was reconstructed, including boundary equality and complex integration; 49,830 finite diagnostics are supporting only.

originality.rationale: The published 2026 Fock recognition theorem and its single-dilation disk criterion are acknowledged as prior. Full-text comparisons distinguish the presently explicit no-cancellation theorem for arbitrary finite sums of distinct centered dilations, exact angular-density law and order-four algebra closure boundary from single-weighted-composition criteria and C*-algebra membership. Searches of published mathematical records and current own-claim deduplication did not reveal an equivalent or stronger covering result. Residual risk: general Fourier recognition could yield this theorem by further argument and two older finite-sum papers could not be read in full.
residual_risks: An equivalent theorem may exist under diagonal moment, Hausdorff moment, or Laplace-transform terminology; semantic search is not a proof of novelty.

value.rationale: This resolves a natural operator-class stability question left open by the sharp individual-dilation Toeplitz disk: forbidden finite dilation contributions cannot cancel into a bounded symbol, and the space of Toeplitz polynomial functions of a compact dilation is an algebra precisely for rotations of orders 1–4. The arbitrary-angle arithmetic density and a sharp phase-transition witness expose nonclosure under squaring, despite every individual good monomial having an explicit bounded Toeplitz symbol. This is a structural classification for an operator family, not an arbitrary numerical slice or single example; it is limited to finite centered dilations.
